payload.chart: Rows x options (pruned cells with reasons): R1 inbound mechanism: (a) POLL the answer topic since a cursor on an interval (ntfy since-poll, probe-confirmed in v1; simple, no inbound port, works behind NAT) | (b) ntfy WebSocket/SSE subscribe (lower latency, but a long-lived connection to manage and reconnect - more surface for an unattended service) | (c) a public webhook the phone service calls back - PRUNED: opens an inbound internet port on the owner's machine, the exact unattended-exposure the excluded list forbids. R2 process host: (a) the answer watcher runs INSIDE the board process (already long-lived, already polling state) | (b) a dedicated watcher process (another thing to supervise via se_ps) | (c) polled on-demand at se_loop_next - PRUNED: adjudication must not depend on the agent calling next; the owner taps asynchronously. R3 module shape: (a) one phone module owning OUTBOUND+INBOUND with the transport injected | (b) two modules (publisher, watcher) sharing a transport - more files for a small lane. R4 transport: (a) an injectable interface, real impl = Node fetch PUT/GET, mock impl in tests (probe A2 confirmed) | (b) shell out to curl - PRUNED: a dependency on an external binary for no gain. R5 correlation id: (a) the offer base_hash verbatim as the id (probe A3) | (b) a separate minted token mapped to the offer - PRUNED: a second secret to store for zero benefit; the hash already IS the unguessable binder. R6 credential home: (a) ~/.se/<project>/phone.json machine-local, never committed (probe A4) | (b) product.json in the repo - PRUNED: a secret in the committed tree, violates req-phone-config-secret.
payload.shortlist: K1 poll-in-board: R1a + R2a + R3a + R4a + R5a + R6a - one phone module, the board process hosts the poll loop, fetch transport injected, offer-hash correlation, machine-local config. K2 poll-dedicated: R1a + R2b + R3b + R4a + R5a + R6a - split publisher/watcher, a dedicated watcher process supervised by se_ps. (K3 push-subscribe R1b considered and kept as the front's second only if latency proves to matter - most likely dominated by K1 on unattended-safety.)
